text: `javac` translates source into instructions for a specified machine that exists only as a document. That machine is the Java ___ Machine.
explanation: Specified rather than built, which is what makes "compile once, run anywhere" possible and what gives Chapter 21 something to look up when it asks what `invokevirtual` does. It is also a stack machine with no registers, chosen partly because that makes bytecode compact and easy to verify, and partly because it bakes in no assumption about how many registers a real processor has.
